intro.headline: Hands-on design leadership for products people have to trust.
intro.sub: I build teams and AI-native design systems that keep quality high.

portfolio.title: Selected work
portfolio.lede: Case studies from Strava, SRAM and SuppCo, each with my role and what changed.

leadership.title: How I lead
leadership.lede: I build the team and the operating system around it: research, rituals, career growth and design systems.

principles.title: Stay in the work
principles.body: I design alongside the team, so my feedback comes from the work, not from a distance.

evidence.text: Led product design as a player-coach, managing one product designer and reporting to the CEO.
Designed StackScore myself, from the first framing through a year of iteration; after launch, an update prompt raised score updates by about a quarter.

principles.title: Unblock the team
principles.body: Design should be a lubricant, not a tollbooth. I keep reviews fast and informal, and build the research, critique and design systems that let people make good calls without me.

evidence.text: Co-led the design team as it grew across Trust & Safety, Growth, Web Platform and Foundations, managing five direct and about ten indirect reports, and promoted designers into staff and management roles.
Led six product designers across the AXS rider app, web, and factory and dealer tools, and hired three in my first six months.
Stood up a research practice: field A/B testing at Sea Otter, and a Dovetail repository that product and engineering adopted.
Made the design system AI-native and packaged it as agent skills in its own repo, so designers, engineers and agents build from one source of truth and following the system no longer runs through me.

principles.title: Judgment is the job
principles.body: Making the hard calls early. Integrity Compass, which I co-created, is one example: it brings privacy, safety and inclusion into the room before launch.

evidence.text: Co-created Integrity Compass, a pre-launch inclusion, privacy and safety review. One session ran nine product teams through it.
Proposed the AXS app’s mission and primary KPI (“Ready to Ride”) to senior leadership, and re-centered the roadmap on the basics riders needed most.

work.title: Crushing the Basics
work.summary: Re-oriented the team around the AXS app’s core value: battery status, firmware updates and connectivity.
work.outcome: I built it on SRAM’s annual rider survey, community votes and support tickets, and sharpened it through 25 stakeholder interviews. It became the product group’s plan for the year.

image.alt: The SRAM AXS app’s battery status for an XX1 rear derailleur: Battery good

work.title: Agentic Design System
work.summary: Made SuppCo’s design system AI-native, so designers, engineers and agents build from one source of truth.
work.outcome: I raised Figma-to-code token parity from 50% to 97% in eight weeks, and packaged the system as agent skills in its own repo.

image.alt: SuppCo’s product card sticker sheet beside the TESTED by SuppCo catalog on iPhone, both built from the design system

work.title: Designing for Trust
work.summary: Redesigned Strava’s privacy controls so athletes could understand, and choose, exactly what they share.
work.outcome: After launch, more than a quarter of active athletes reviewed the new controls, and 27% of them changed a setting.

image.alt: Strava privacy controls: the privacy settings list, profile page visibility, and the Heatmap opt-out

work.title: Surfacing Value
work.summary: A strategic redesign of Strava’s information architecture and navigation, for clarity, scale and growth.
work.outcome: I facilitated the sprint. 84% of subscribers said they understood what had changed, and the experiment showed a net gain in bookings after counting downgrades.

image.alt: Three screens from Strava’s redesigned navigation: the new home feed, introducing Maps, and competing and connecting with others

work.title: StackScore
work.summary: Redesigned SuppCo’s signature score into a hub that explains itself and tells members what to do next.
work.role: Designer (product and engineering owned the scoring logic)
work.outcome: I designed a score-update prompt; after launch, score updates rose by about a quarter for both free and Pro members.

image.alt: SuppCo StackScore app screens: the score overview ring, Quality tab, and Goals tab

work.title: Buying Club
work.summary: Co-designed SuppCo’s first commerce product, a members’ club that sells trusted supplements without discounts.
work.role: Shared design ownership with the Head of Product
work.outcome: Alpha told us the checkout worked and the catalog was the constraint.

image.alt: The Buying Club on desktop, “the new way to buy supplements,” beside the onboarding screen where members earn 30% back in credits

about.title: Hi, I’m Andy.

photo.alt: Andy Detskas walking up the steps of a sunlit, whitewashed courtyard

about.body: I lead design for products people have to trust: privacy and safety at Strava, connected bikes at SRAM, and supplement trust at SuppCo (acquired by Function Health). Before I led teams, I was a hands-on designer at Pivotal Labs, Punchkick Interactive and DePaul University, and I still do the work myself.
about.more: For inspiration, I love to watch movies, travel and shoot photos, and spend time learning about the craftsmanship that goes into building watches and bikes. I love creative endeavors that blend the technical and creative.

experience.role: Senior Staff Product Designer / Senior Product Design Manager

about.next: I’m looking for a Senior Design Manager role leading five to eight designers, ideally in design systems or trust and safety. I’m in Denver, and open to remote, hybrid, or relocation.
